Subject: SLA request: async batch completion windows & idempotency

Hi Priyom / Dev,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our SRE and procurement teams have two primary concerns we need Redwood to commit to in the contract:

1) Completion windows for asynchronous/batch inference jobs (we run large nightly scoring that occasionally produces long-tail jobs). We need a clear SLO and remedy for jobs that exceed the window.
2) Idempotency and retry semantics — if we retry a job due to a transient error, we need strong dedup guarantees and transparent behavior for partial outputs.

Specific asks from our side: can Redwood provide a proposal that includes:
- A target completion SLO (e.g., % of jobs completed within X hours) with clear definitions (what counts as a job, how time-to-complete is measured).
- Retry/backoff policies and whether Redwood supports client-provided job_id dedup tokens or server-assigned ids.
- Handling of poisoned/failed jobs and whether there is a dead-letter queue or manual intervention process.
- Credit/remedy calculations for missed completion SLAs (simple example in dollars or %).

Procurement timeline is tight — we'd like a draft SLA by Tue (20 Apr). I've attached our vendor questionnaire for reference.

Best,

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. We can have a concrete proposal by Tue 20 Apr. High level up-front:

- Measurement: we define a job as a single submitted async inference request identified by job_id that returns a final status (succeeded/failed/cancelled). Completion time is measured from submission timestamp to final terminal state.
- Option A (conservative): 99.5% of jobs completed within 24 hours; remedied by pro-rata credits tied to SLA band breaches.
- Option B (performance tier): 99% within 6 hours for jobs under 500k tokens, 99.9% within 24 hours for all jobs (requires Dedicated capacity or reserved throughput).
- Idempotency: support client-provided job_id for dedup; if omitted, Redwood will issue a UUID and expose it in the job response. Dedup window default 72 hours (configurable). Retries are safe within the dedup window.
- Poisoned jobs: job moves to a failed state after N attempts (configurable, default 5), then flagged for manual review. We provide a dead-letter queue with a runbook for recovery.

I've attached a short runbook and a formal proposal draft (pdf). Dev — can you add technical SLO definitions and wording for contract carveouts (force majeure, model downgrade, planned maintenance)? Evelyn — procurement wants suggested credit math.

Quick technical write-up / proposed contract language snippets:

1) Definitions:
- "Job": a single async inference submission (single payload) regardless of number of model invocations.
- "Completion": terminal state (Succeeded / Failed / Cancelled) and all outputs written to the configured result store. Partial outputs flagged as "partial_success" do not count as completed for SLA purposes unless the customer configured incremental flush semantics.

2) Measurement windows & SLOs (recommended defaults):
- SLO 1 (Standard Hosted): 99.5% of jobs completed within 24 hours measured across a monthly calendar window.
- SLO 2 (Performance Reserved): 99% of jobs under 500k tokens completed within 6 hours; 99.9% of all jobs within 24 hours when on Dedicated capacity.

3) Idempotency & retries:
- We honor client-provided job_id for dedup. If no job_id, server issues job_id and returns it synchronously.
- Dedup window: 72 hours default (configurable to 7 days for enterprise customers).
- Retries: exponential backoff (base 30s, max 1h) for transient errors; middleware will suppress duplicate work if job_id matches and prior job is in flight or completed.

4) Failure modes & poison handling:
- After 5 failed attempts (configurable), job is moved to Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) and marked "requires manual review".
- Customers can opt into automatic compensation runs (reprocess with higher memory/longer timeout) for DLQ items; otherwise, manual troubleshooting.

5) Remedies & credits:
- Simple credit model proposal for procurement: For each calendar month, if monthly completion rate falls between 99.0-99.5%, customer receives 10% service credit of monthly invoice; 98.0-99.0% => 25% credit; below 98% => 50% credit and escalation to account team. Credits capped at 50% per month.

6) Contract carveouts (suggested):
- Force majeure, scheduled maintenance with >72 hours notice, third-party model provider outage, exfil/cyber incidents.

Metrics & telemetry: We will publish a per-job completion histogram, 95/99/100th percentile completion times, DLQ counts, and idempotency collisions.

Tagging: suggest we add a clause allowing BrightEdge to request an SLA review after two months of production telemetry.
